seo.title: Our Story | P K Guled Ilkal Sarees since 1875
seo.description: The P K Guled story: a family of Ilkal saree makers since 1875. Learn about Ilkal handloom weaving, the Tope Teni pallu and the Kondi technique.

hero.heading: Since 1875. Still at the same looms.
hero.lead: P K Guled began weaving Ilkal sarees in 1875. Today we are the oldest saree house in Ilkal, working with local weaver families to keep the Tope Teni pallu and Kasuti traditions alive.

sections.heading: A saree named after its town
paragraphs: Ilkal is a weaving town in Bagalkote district, Karnataka, and the sarees woven here carry its name. Silk, silk-cotton and cotton sarees are woven on handlooms by local weaver families.
Small slubs and yarn variations are the fingerprint of a handloom. No two sarees are identical.

image.alt: Weaver at the handloom in Ilkal

sections.heading: The signature of an Ilkal saree
paragraphs: The classic temple-pattern pallu, joined to the body with the traditional Kondi technique.
In the Kondi technique the pallu is woven separately and then joined to the body of the saree with interlocking loops of yarn, so the join is part of the weave itself.

image.alt: Close-up of a Tope Teni pallu

sections.heading: Care guide with every order
paragraphs: Dry clean for silk. Hand wash cotton with reetha powder to keep colours rich for years.
